fields.name: Execution Prompt - Single Feature
fields.description:
Please generate an implementation plan for <insert Feature>, it's downstream Requirements. ONLY use requirements that have a status of "Approved" if the requirements do not have an approved status, skip them during development.

 

Do not run diagnostics, and do not build any testing plans for this development. Testing will be manually completed by the user.

 

Upon completion of the development, create an Implementation Summary in the Implementation Summaries Set. The Name field populated as: <insert Feature> Date and Time of development. Add the following into the Description field:

  • Implementation Plan
  • Tasks
  • Walkthrough

Please relate the created Implementation Summary to the <insert Feature> item and its related downstream Requirements that were used in this development. If a requirement was skipped during development for not being approved, do not relate it.

 

If there were any issues with development, for example, something that could not be coded for a given reason, create a Defect with the Name field populated as <insert Feature> <short keyword description of Defect>. In the Description field, please include a summary of what failed or went wrong and the next steps for the user to take. Please relate the defect to all affected Features, Requirements, and Test Cases.

fields.name: Execution Prompt - All Features
fields.description:
Please generate an implementation plan for all SDD Features that are in the Approved Status, and Text Items in the Features Set. This includes all downstream SDD Requirements from each SDD Feature. ONLY use requirements that have a status of "Approved" if the requirements do not have an approved status, skip them during development. If a SDD Feature is not approved, list it as skipped and skip all of its downstream requirements, regardless of their stats.

 

Upon completion of the development, create an SDD Implementation Summary in the SDD Implementation Summaries Set. The Name field populated as: Date and Time of development. Add the following into the Description field:

  • Implementation Plan
    • Include a table of requirements impacted and requirements skipped
  • Tasks
  • Walkthrough

Please relate the created SDD Implementation Summary to all SDD Features and their related downstream SDD Requirements that were used in this development. If a requirement was skipped during development for not being approved, do not relate it.

 

If there were any issues with development, for example, something that could not be coded for a given reason, create a Defect with the Name field populated as <insert SDD Feature> & <Insert Specific SDD Requirement> <short keyword description of Defect>. In the Description field, please include a summary of what failed or went wrong and the next steps for the user to take. Please relate the defect to all affected SDD Features, SDD Requirements, and SDD Verifications.

fields.name: Generate Features and Requirements From Code
fields.description:
INTRODUCTION

This execution prompt is designed to help facilitate the reverse engineering of features and requirements for a code base. The end goal is to create features and requirements that are missing from the current requirements set within the Jama project that has been identified. By creating these items, a code base will be completely defined by the features and requirement specification stored in Jama Connect.

 

FEATURE FORMAT

The following defines the format for each feature generated.

  • Features must have a short, meaningful, name that the user will understand the general functionality that is being described by the feature.
  • Each feature must have a descriptive paragraph or two defining the overall functionality that the requirements related to the feature detail.
  • Newly generated features by this execution prompt must have a status of draft.
  • Newly generated features by this execution prompt must be created within the Features set [TAF1APP-SET-1] and within the AI Generated folder [TAF1APP-FLD-23].
  • Newly generated features must relate to the generated requirements associated with the.

REQUIREMENT FORMAT

The following defines the format for each requirement generated.

  • Each requirement must have a short, meaningful, name that the user will understand the general required functionality that is being defined by the requirement.
    • For requirements used as definitions, the name must being with "DEFINITION: ".
  • The requirements generated must follow this standard format: The application shall <active action verb> <action> <optional parameter or criteria>.
  • The requirements generated must relate to only ONE feature.
  • The requirements generated may relate to newly AI Generated features or existing Human Generated features that already reside in the project.
  • Requirements must be grouped together within Requirements set [TAF1APP-SET-2] within the AI Generated folder [TAF1APP-FLD-25] within the Requirements folder [TAF1APP-FLD-27] within a folder that matches the name of the upstream feature for that requirement.
    • The exception to this is when the requirement is being used as a definition, which means they must be housed under the Requirements Set within the AI Generated folder within the Definitions folder [TAF1APP-FLD-26].

PROCESS

  1. The AI agent shall review the current list of features in the specified Jama project.
  2. The AI agent shall compare the current list of features in the specified Jama project against the existing codebase.
  3. The AI agent shall review the current list of requirements in the specified Jama project.
  4. The AI agent shall compare the current list of requirements in the specified Jama project against the existing codebase.
  5. The AI agent shall provide the user a list of features and requirements it plans to generated within an Implementation Plan (if there is a .md file specifying the approach for this, ensure it is followed).
  6. The AI agent shall, once approved to proceed by the user, generate a baseline of the specified Jama Connect project (from the project top level, not the individual sets) which includes all items within that project.
  7. The AI agent shall title the first baseline in the following way: "Pre-Generate Features and Requirements <date> <time>".
  8. The AI agent shall, once approved to proceed by the user, create the features and requirements, along with relationships between each feature and its associated requirements in Jama Connect.
  9. The AI agent shall generate an Implementation Summary and relate it to the features and requirements generated during this execution, with the following information included:
    • A copy paste of the implementation plan generated that the user approved
    • A copy paste of the tasks file created
    • A copy paste of the walkthrough file created
  10. The AI agent shall generate a baseline of the specified Jama Connect project (from the project top level, not the individual sets) which includes all items within that project.
  11. The AI agent shall title the second baseline in the following way: "Post-Generate Features and Requirements <date> <time>".

fields.name: Jama Item Launch and User Session
fields.description:
Open the hardware viewer in the context of the Jama item selected by the user. Validate the launching instance and project, obtain the active user's delegated session, and retain that session only for the current browser interaction. Clear protected content when Jama rejects access and prevent stale asynchronous responses from restoring data from a previous run or session.

Implementation evidence: frontend/app.js, frontend/transport.js, src/jama_model_viewer/server.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F01. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Embedded Workspace and Appearance
fields.description:
Present the viewer inline in Jama and offer a larger view using the host's native drawer contract. Keep user-facing item and revision information visible, provide clear loading and error messages, and support a locally remembered light, dark, or system appearance without persisting Jama content.

Implementation evidence: frontend/index.html, frontend/app.js, frontend/viewer.css. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F02. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Interactive Model Viewing
fields.description:
Display one or more published GLB or 3MF model previews with independent controls. Let the user freely rotate the camera and rotate each model explicitly around X, Y, and Z, while retaining fit/reset and standard viewpoints. Load models on demand and release renderer resources when the selected run changes.

Implementation evidence: frontend/model.js, frontend/app.js, frontend/transport.js, src/jama_model_viewer/core.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F03. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: GIF Animation Playback
fields.description:
Show published GIF animations with an initial still poster and explicit playback controls. Keep the single-animation view compact, group multiple animations in independent nested sections, and stop playback when the relevant section is closed or the page is hidden.

Implementation evidence: frontend/app.js, src/jama_model_viewer/publisher.py, src/jama_model_viewer/core.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F04. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Published Run Discovery and Downloads
fields.description:
Resolve complete publications belonging to the selected Jama item and let the user choose between retained runs. Retrieve the original asset bytes for rendering or download while preventing files from different instances, projects, items, or runs from being combined.

Implementation evidence: frontend/app.js, frontend/transport.js, src/jama_model_viewer/service.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F05. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Artifact Package Preparation
fields.description:
Prepare a reproducible viewer package from exported model files and optional source CAD and GIFs after the existing summary publication has finished. Capture the source requirements snapshot and file hashes so changed inputs cannot be silently published as the prepared run. Produce posters automatically and validate local filenames and supported encodings before writes.

Implementation evidence: src/jama_model_viewer/publisher.py, src/jama_model_viewer/core.py, src/jama_model_viewer/cli.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F06. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Resumable Jama Publication
fields.description:
Publish viewer attachments onto the verified existing summary as a separate operation from model generation and summary creation. Support read-only preflight, resumable per-file state, verified uploads and associations, and a final manifest association that makes the complete run discoverable. Stop on unresolved write outcomes rather than duplicating Jama items.

Implementation evidence: src/jama_model_viewer/publisher.py, src/jama_model_viewer/cli.py, src/jama_model_viewer/jama_rest.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F07. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Protected Attachment Access
fields.description:
Keep Jama user permissions authoritative for model and animation access. Restrict the adapter to bounded reads against the configured Jama instance, validate exact item and attachment bindings, and prevent the read endpoints from becoming a general proxy. Return useful access errors without logging user tokens or customer content.

Implementation evidence: src/jama_model_viewer/service.py, src/jama_model_viewer/server.py, frontend/transport.js. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F08. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Jama ZIP Storage Compatibility
fields.description:
Store model, source CAD, and manifest files in genuine ZIP containers when their original extensions are unsuitable for direct Jama attachment upload. Preserve original filenames and hashes for user downloads, validate the stored container separately, and bound extraction to the single declared file. Continue reading earlier direct-file publications.

Implementation evidence: src/jama_model_viewer/archive.py, src/jama_model_viewer/publisher.py, src/jama_model_viewer/service.py, frontend/archive.js, frontend/transport.js. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F09. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Local STEP Preview Conversion
fields.description:
Convert an exported STEP model into an embedded GLB mesh using the locally bundled OCCT importer. Keep conversion outside the viewing service, normalize coordinates for the viewer, and record the settings and limitations of the resulting visualization. Preserve the original source as the engineering reference.

Implementation evidence: scripts/convert-step.cjs, frontend/step-to-glb.cjs, README.md. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F10. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Offline Deployment and Release Packaging
fields.description:
Provide the same viewer assets for a native customer-hosted adapter or a qualified static deployment. Bundle browser libraries and offline installation dependencies, expose local health checks, and package releases from selected source locations. Keep rendering in the browser and document the HTTPS, browser permission, and Jama registration prerequisites separately from model generation.

Implementation evidence: src/jama_model_viewer/server.py, src/jama_model_viewer/service.py, scripts/build_release.py, scripts/bundle_vendor.py, scripts/verify.py, docs/deployment.md. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F11. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.

fields.name: Legacy Package Compatibility
fields.description:
Read previously published manifests without restoring the drawing user interface that was removed at the user's request. Preserve compatibility options needed by older automation while keeping the current viewer limited to models, source downloads, and GIF animations.

Implementation evidence: frontend/index.html, frontend/app.js, src/jama_model_viewer/core.py, src/jama_model_viewer/cli.py, src/jama_model_viewer/drawing.py. Generated from the approved JCTK-TXT-5 plan for Hardware-Model-Viewer; reference F12. Status reflects a code-derived Draft specification, not independent acceptance verification.
